title: Malta Year 7 Math — Year 7 (Short) Unit 1 to Unit 3 Recap
question: Can place value, LCM, powers, BIDMAS, fractions, proportion, sequences, brackets and equations from Year 7 Units 1 to 3 be applied in nine short questions?
intro: Three questions for each unit. **Show your working before choosing A–D.**

questions.title: Unit 1 · Place value
questions.prompt: What is the value of the digit 7 in 3,742,105?
questions.solution: Reading from the left: 3 millions, 7 hundred-thousands, 4 ten-thousands, so the 7 is worth 700,000.

questions.title: Unit 1 · LCM
questions.prompt: Ferries to Comino leave every 20 minutes and boat trips leave every 30 minutes. Both leave at 9:00. When do they next leave together?
questions.solution:
Multiples of 30: 30, 60, … and 60 is the first that 20 divides, so they meet again 60 minutes later, at 10:00.

\[\text{LCM}(20, 30) = 60\]

9:50 adds the two times, and 19:00 uses \(20\times30 = 600\) minutes — a common multiple, but not the lowest.

questions.title: Unit 1 · Powers, decimals, negatives
questions.solution: \(0.07 = \frac{7}{100} = 7\%\). The others are false: \(2^3 = 8\), \(4^2 = 16\), and \(-8 < -3\) because \(-8\) is further left on the number line.

questions.title: Unit 2 · BIDMAS
questions.solution_title: Indices, then ÷ and × left to right
questions.solution:
\[36\div4\times3 - 2^2 = 9\times3 - 4 = 27 - 4 = \boxed{23}\]

−1 comes from doing \(4\times3\) before the division; 25 treats \(2^2\) as 2.

questions.title: Unit 2 · Fractions
questions.solution:
\[\frac34\times\frac29 = \frac{6}{36} = \boxed{\frac16}\]

\(\frac{5}{13}\) adds tops and bottoms; \(\frac{27}{8}\) is the answer to a division.

questions.title: Unit 2 · Direct proportion
questions.prompt: 5 kg of oranges cost €6.50. What do 8 kg cost?
questions.solution:
\[6.50\div5 = 1.30, \qquad 8\times1.30 = \boxed{10.40}\]

So 8 kg cost €10.40. €9.50 adds €3 for 3 more kg instead of €1.30 per kg.

questions.title: Unit 3 · Sequences
questions.prompt: What is the nth term of 5, 8, 11, 14, …?
questions.solution:
The step is 3, so the rule starts with \(3n\). At \(n = 1\), \(3n = 3\), and the first term is 5, so add 2: \(3n + 2\).

\(3n + 5\) uses the first term instead of the adjustment; it gives 8 for \(n = 1\).

questions.title: Unit 3 · Brackets
questions.solution_title: Multiply both terms in the bracket

questions.title: Unit 3 · Equations
questions.solution:
\[4x = 28 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x = 7\]

Check: \(4\times7 + 9 = 37\). 11.5 adds 9 instead of subtracting it; 28 stops before dividing by 4.

takeaway: Order matters: compare place value from the left, do × and ÷ from left to right, and undo the operations of an equation in reverse order.
